questions.q: How did Fogg spend most of the afternoon at the Reform Club?
choices: Reading the Times and then the Standard
Playing billiards with the club's bankers
Writing letters in the club's law library
Walking slowly in the club's autumn garden
questions.evidence: The perusal of this paper absorbed Phileas Fogg until a quarter before four

questions.q: Which of these men was one of Fogg's usual whist partners and a Director of the Bank of England?
choices: Andrew Stuart
Gauthier Ralph
Thomas Flanagan
John Sullivan
questions.evidence: Gauthier Ralph, one of the Directors of the Bank of England

questions.q: How much money had been stolen from the Bank of England?
choices: Twenty thousand pounds
Four thousand pounds
Fifty-five thousand pounds
Two thousand pounds
questions.evidence: A package of banknotes, to the value of fifty-five thousand pounds

questions.q: What was the principal cashier doing when the banknotes were taken from his table?
choices: Counting gold ingots in the back room
Recording a payment of three shillings and sixpence
Talking with Gauthier Ralph about the day's business
Locking the doors of the bank at five o'clock
questions.evidence: registering the receipt of three shillings and sixpence

questions.q: What point does the story about the gold ingot being passed from hand to hand make?
choices: The Bank trusts the public and barely guards its treasures
Gold ingots in the Bank are much lighter than most people believe
The cashiers at the Bank watch every visitor with very great care
Visitors to the Bank often try to steal the gold that they hold
questions.evidence: the Bank of England reposes a touching confidence in the honesty of the public

questions.q: What reward was offered to the detectives who caught the thief?
choices: Two thousand pounds and five per cent of the sum recovered
Twenty thousand pounds paid by the directors of the Bank of England
A place as a director of the Bank of England
Half of all the stolen banknotes they recovered
questions.evidence: the proffered reward of two thousand pounds, and five per cent.

questions.q: Who had been seen walking to and fro in the paying room on the day of the robbery?
choices: A shabby sailor who had just come from Liverpool
A well-dressed gentleman of polished manners
A young clerk who had recently been dismissed
A group of men from a professional band of thieves
questions.evidence: a well-dressed gentleman of polished manners

questions.q: Why did Ralph believe the detectives would probably catch the thief?
choices: He knew the thief's real name and address
He thought the prize would stimulate their zeal
He had hired the best detective in London himself
He believed the thief was still hiding inside the Bank
questions.evidence: he thought that the prize offered would greatly stimulate their zeal and activity

questions.q: Fogg says the world "was once" big enough. What does he mean?
choices: People can now travel around it much faster than before
Many small countries have joined together into one great empire
Maps of the world used to show more land than there is
Most of the world has now been explored and settled
questions.evidence: a man can now go round it ten times more quickly than a hundred years ago

questions.q: Why did John Sullivan say the trip could now be made in only eighty days?
choices: A new steamer line had begun sailing from Suez
A new section of railway in India had been opened
A canal across America had just been finished
The trains to Dover had been made twice as fast
questions.evidence: now that the section between Rothal and Allahabad, on the Great Indian Peninsula Railway, has been opened

questions.q: Each time Stuart named a danger like bad weather or shipwreck, how did Fogg answer?
choices: "All included"
"Quite impossible"
"Deal over again"
"Only a joke"

questions.q: How much money did Fogg bet that he could go around the world in eighty days?
choices: Four thousand pounds
Twenty thousand pounds
Fifty-five thousand pounds
Forty thousand pounds
questions.evidence: I have a deposit of twenty thousand at Baring's which I will willingly risk upon it.

questions.q: Fogg says, "The unforeseen does not exist." What does unforeseen mean?
choices: Something that is very costly
Something nobody expected ahead of time
Something that is hidden from everyone's view
Something that happens far away

questions.q: By what day and time must Fogg be back in the Reform Club to win the bet?
choices: Saturday, the 21st of December, at a quarter before nine p.m.
Wednesday, the 2nd of October, at a quarter before nine p.m.
Sunday, the 22nd of December, exactly at midnight in London
Saturday, the 21st of December, at half-past eleven a.m.
questions.evidence: on Saturday, the 21st of December, at a quarter before nine p.m.

questions.q: Why did Fogg bet only half of his fortune?
choices: He did not trust the other men to pay if they lost
He expected to need the other half to pay for the trip
He had promised the other half to his favourite charities
He was keeping the other half to pay his new servant
questions.evidence: because he foresaw that he might have to expend the other half

questions.q: What is the most important thing that happens in this chapter?
choices: The thief who robbed the Bank of England is finally caught
Fogg bets his club friends he can go around the world in eighty days
Fogg loses half of his whole fortune in a long game of whist at the club
The detectives at the ports are given a description of the thief
questions.evidence: I will bet twenty thousand pounds against anyone who wishes
